cases_doc: D.3 calibration slate — homology_search (BLAST+HMMER). Line: significance vs homology (C1-hole H5).
label_provenance: pre-registered by the build chat 2026-07-19 from the ruled card (H1-H5); in->trust, out->defer.
substrate_text: BLAST / HMMER local sequence-homology search against a validly-built database, with Karlin-Altschul e-value statistics. FILTER-class: the e-value is the SIGNIFICANCE of similarity, a relative screen — NOT homology, orthology, or function. The tool field selects the backend {blast, hmmer}. Returns the best (min) e-value ONLY when the search provably ran (a valid database, no error); a clean run with 0 hits is a real 'no significant homolog', DISTINCT from a search that could not run. THE KNOWN GAP (H5): a significant e-value is statistical significance of SIMILARITY, not homology/function; low-complexity and composition bias inflate significance; a profile-HMM (HMMER) detects remote homology a raw pairwise e-value cannot speak to.
envelope_text: IN-REGIME: a genuinely significant hit read as SIGNIFICANCE (a similarity screen against a valid DB). OUT-OF-REGIME: a claim of biological HOMOLOGY/orthology/function derived from the e-value; a claim about REMOTE homology a pairwise e-value cannot detect; an absolute-homology assertion; a significant hit driven by low-complexity bias read as real similarity.

gate_cases.experiment: Search a query protein against the database with blast and report the best-hit e-value as the statistical SIGNIFICANCE of the sequence similarity found.
gate_cases.note: Dead-centre: a similarity search read as significance — exactly the screen the card gates on.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the BLAST e-value read as similarity significance.

gate_cases.experiment: Search a query against the database with blast; report a strongly significant e-value (well below the stated threshold) as evidence of a significant sequence match.
gate_cases.note: In-regime: e-value below threshold read as a significant match — the trust path.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the BLAST e-value below threshold, as a significant similarity.

gate_cases.experiment: Use hmmer (profile search) against the database and report the best full-sequence e-value as the significance of the profile match.
gate_cases.note: In-regime: the HMMER significance of a profile match, read as significance.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the HMMER profile-search e-value, as match significance.

gate_cases.experiment: Report that a query with a best-hit e-value ABOVE the stated threshold has NO significant homolog in the database at that cutoff (a clean no-hit result).
gate_cases.note: In-regime: a clean 'no significant hit at this cutoff' is a real, trustworthy result of the similarity screen.
gate_cases.right_instrument: the search's honest 'no significant hit at this cutoff'.

gate_cases.experiment: Rank two candidate query sequences against the database by their best-hit e-values as a RELATIVE similarity-significance screen.
gate_cases.note: In-regime: a relative significance ranking — the filter's intended use.
gate_cases.right_instrument: two BLAST e-values compared relatively for similarity significance.

gate_cases.experiment: From a significant BLAST e-value, conclude that the query protein IS a functional homolog (an ortholog with the same molecular function) of the database hit.
gate_cases.note: C1-hole H5, direct: e-value is similarity significance, NOT homology/function. Concluding function from an e-value is out-of-envelope.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a homology/orthology + functional-annotation analysis — not an e-value.

gate_cases.experiment: Use a BLAST pairwise e-value to detect REMOTE homology between two distantly related sequences with no significant pairwise similarity.
gate_cases.note: Out of regime: remote homology is what a raw pairwise e-value cannot detect (H5); it needs a profile/structure method.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a profile-HMM or structural method for remote homology — not a pairwise e-value.

gate_cases.experiment: Report a low e-value driven by a low-complexity (repeat-rich) region as evidence of true biological similarity.
gate_cases.note: C1-hole H5: low-complexity/composition bias inflates significance; the hit is not real similarity.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a low-complexity-filtered analysis — the raw e-value is biased here.

gate_cases.experiment: State that the best-hit e-value proves the two sequences share a common evolutionary ancestor (asserting homology as established fact).
gate_cases.note: C1-hole H5: an absolute-homology/evolutionary-ancestry claim; the e-value is significance of similarity, not proof of homology.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a phylogenetic/evolutionary analysis — not a similarity e-value.

gate_cases.experiment: From a significant e-value against a partial database, conclude the query has NO other homologs anywhere in nature (absolute completeness).
gate_cases.note: Out of regime: an absolute/completeness claim beyond the searched database — the e-value speaks only to the DB searched.
gate_cases.right_instrument: a comprehensive/complete search — a single DB e-value cannot support completeness.

wrapper_cases.note: hmmer query must be a baked profile, not a sequence.
